tagline: Deliver Jira sprint updates and issue alerts directly in Microsoft Teams
metaTitle: Jira and Microsoft Teams: Automated Notifications by Project
metaDescription: Post sprint digests, urgent escalations, and release notes from each Jira project to its own Teams channel. GAIA answers Jira questions. See the setup steps.
intro:
Microsoft Teams is the enterprise communication standard for organizations running on Microsoft 365, and Jira is the enterprise issue tracker of choice for software teams. Despite how often they're used together, keeping everyone informed of project progress requires either manual posting or a limited built-in connector that lacks contextual formatting and intelligent routing.

GAIA provides a richer connection between the two. Sprint summaries, blocker alerts, release notifications, and high-priority issue escalations are posted to the right channels with structured, readable formatting. Non-technical stakeholders can query GAIA in Teams for project status without needing a Jira license. Engineering managers receive personalized digests of their team's sprint progress.

For large enterprises where chat is the operational hub, issue data reaches the right people in the right channels with the right context — automatically.

useCases.title: Daily sprint status digest
useCases.description: GAIA posts a morning sprint status digest to the engineering channel showing yesterday's completions, today's planned work, and any open blockers requiring immediate attention.

useCases.title: High-priority issue escalation alerts
useCases.description: When a ticket is raised to Blocker or Critical priority, GAIA posts an alert to the team's channel and tags the assignee and engineering lead for immediate response.

useCases.title: Release notification to stakeholder channels
useCases.description: When a sprint or version is released, GAIA posts a formatted release announcement to the designated channel listing all resolved issues, suitable for sharing with business stakeholders.

useCases.title: Jira queries answered in Teams
useCases.description: Stakeholders can ask GAIA in chat, 'What's the status of the payments project?' or 'Is the login bug fixed yet?', and receive an accurate, real-time answer sourced from Jira.

useCases.title: New issue assignment notifications
useCases.description: When an issue is assigned to a team member, GAIA sends them a Teams message with the issue summary, priority, due date, and sprint assignment so they're immediately aware of new work.

howItWorks.step: Connect Jira and Microsoft Teams to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authenticate your Jira instance and install the GAIA app in your Microsoft Teams organization. Map projects to the channels where notifications should be delivered.
Define which events generate notifications, issue assignments, priority escalations, sprint events, deployments, and configure the format and routing for each event type.

howItWorks.step: GAIA notifies channels and responds to queries
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors the projects continuously and posts structured notifications in real time. Team members can also query GAIA directly in chat for live project status.

faqs.question: Can GAIA post to a different channel for each project?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can configure a separate channel for each project or board. GAIA routes notifications to the appropriate channel automatically based on the issue's project assignment.

faqs.question: Can Teams users create issues without a Jira account?
faqs.answer: Yes. Users can ask GAIA in a chat message to create an issue, providing a description and priority. GAIA creates the issue under the appropriate project and returns the link.

faqs.question: Does GAIA support Adaptive Cards for issue notifications?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA formats notifications as Adaptive Cards, including issue summary, priority indicator, assignee, sprint name, and action buttons to transition issue status without leaving the channel.

faqs.question: How is this different from the standard built-in connector?
faqs.answer: The standard connector sends basic webhook notifications. GAIA adds AI-powered filtering, intelligent routing, natural language queries, and two-way actions (like creating or updating issues) directly from the channel.
